To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the acidic catalase activity in the stratum corneum is associated with the clinically defined skin type; 2) acidic catalase in the stratum comesum is not associated with the skin pigmentation; and 3) acidic catalase is not associated with sun exposure history.
(a) the rs910873 marker is associated with malignant melanoma (MM), (b) the rs1885120 marker is associated with MM, and (c) both markers are associated with MM.

‘The rs910873 and the rs1885120 single-nucleotide polymorphisms on chromosome 20q11.22, which are associated with malignant melanoma in the general population, are also significantly associated with malignant melanomas that develop on sun-exposed skin.’
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis for the development of malignant melanoma.
the genetic basis for melanoma susceptibility and the role of chromosome 20 markers in melanoma.
the association between the rs910873 (rs1885120) markers in the 20q12 region and melanoma risk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acidic catalase is a marker of cutaneous photo-susceptibility in low phototype Caucasian individuals.
‘this study showed the existence of an association of acidic catalase with clinically defined risk in low phototype Caucasian skin, which contributes to the knowledge of cutaneous photosensitivity.’
the acidic catalase is associated with the cutaneous photosuspectibility, but the association needs more investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acidic catalase is a new marker of photosusceptibility, and it is associated with the risk factors for cutaneous photosusensitivity in vivo.
acidic catalase is a marker of cutaneous condition, not a marker of cutaneos photosusceptibility.
the association of the acidic catalase with the skin phototypes and the skin cancer is not as strong as Vittoria et al. [1] claimed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rs910873 marker on 20q12 is modestly associated with melanoma.
the association of the rs910873 marker with malignant melanoma is not as strong as previously suggested [2].

the rs910873 marker on chromosome 20 is modestly associated with the risk of malignant melanoma (odds ratio, 1.17; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-1.36) and the rs1885120 marker is associated with the risk (odds ratio 1.19; 95% CI 1.02-1.39) [2].
